rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A person’s allotted good and evil remain attached to him wherever he goes.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وما قدر عليه

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Good and evil accompany a person until he is reckoned for them.
rows.anchor: الكلبي ومقاتل: خيره وشره معه لا يفارقه حتى يحاسب به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan recites that recording angels sit at a person’s right and left; his open record accompanies him through life, is folded at death, and reopened at resurrection.
rows.anchor: وتلا الحسن: عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد] ثم قال يا بن آدم بسطت لك صحيفتك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The attached bird signifies a person’s deeds and provision.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: عمله ورزقه، وعنه: ما من مولود يولد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Every newborn has a paper at his neck recording whether he is blessed or wretched.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: عمله ورزقه، وعنه: ما من مولود يولد إلا وفي عنقه ورقة

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The bird represents what a person is destined to do and become, whether happy or wretched.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: أراد بالطائر ما قضى عليه

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The destiny is called a bird by analogy with Arab omens drawn from birds flying to the right or left.
rows.anchor: وإنما عبر عنه بالطائر على عادة العرب كما كانت تتفاءل به

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد والعيني
rows.claim: The bird means one’s share of good or evil, as in the Arab idiom that someone’s bird flew with a certain lot.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيد والعيني: أراد بالطائر حظه من الخير والشر

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: They read طئره without the alif; the neck is singled out because marks and ornaments are placed there and Arabs assign lasting things to the neck.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء: طئره في عنقه بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The neck is singled out as the place of marks, necklaces, and things that adorn or disfigure, matching Arab idioms for an inescapable duty.
rows.anchor: لأن العنق موضع السمات وموضع القلائد والأطراف وغير ذلك مما يشين أو يزين

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وابن محيصن ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read ويخرج with open yāʾ and damma on rāʾ, making the person’s bird bring out a book; كتابًا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن ومجاهد وابن محيصن ويعقوب: ويخرج بفتح الياء وضم الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative construal has the person’s bird emerge and become a book.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون معناه ويخرج له الطائر فيصير كتابا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the verb passively, meaning that the bird is brought out as a book.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: ويخرج بضم الياء وفتح الراء

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads an active form with God as its understood subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب: ويخرج أي ويخرج الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use first-person plural and take كتابًا as the object; Abū ʿAmr supports this from ألزمناه, though the citation is cut off.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بنون مضمومة وكسر الراء على معنى ونحن نخرج له

rows.speaker: أبو عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: They read تلقاه with tāʾ and doubled qāf, meaning the person is given the book; others use yāʾ, meaning he sees it.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عامر وأبو جعفر: تلقاه بضم التاء وتشديد القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منشورًا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative, describing the book as open.
rows.anchor: منشورا نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: أبو السوار العدوي
rows.claim: A person’s record is open in life, folded at death, and reopened at resurrection, so he should fill it as he chooses while alive.
rows.anchor: يا ابن آدم فصحيفتك منشورة فاعمل فيها ما شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is told to read his book; he himself suffices as his reckoner and requiter.
rows.anchor: اقرأ كتابك يعني فيقال له اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: On that day even a person who did not act as his own reckoner in worldly life will read his record.
rows.anchor: قتادة: سيقرأ يومئذ كل من لم يكن في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: God has acted justly by making each person his own reckoner.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: [قد عدل والله عليك] من جعلك حسيب نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits the guided person, while misguidance brings punishment upon the one who strays.
rows.anchor: من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه لها نوليه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No bearer of sin carries another person’s sin.
rows.anchor: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ولا يحمل حامله عمل أخر من الأثام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not punish until a messenger establishes proof with signs that remove the people’s excuse.
rows.anchor: وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا إقامة للحجة عليهم بالآيات

rows.speaker: عثمان النهدي وأبو رجاء العطاردي وأبو العالية وأبو جعفر ومجاهد
rows.claim: They read أمرنا with doubled mīm, glossed as mixing in or setting the wicked among a town’s people, after which they disobey and are destroyed.
rows.anchor: قرأ عثمان النهدي وأبو رجاء العطاردي وأبو العالية [وأبو جعفر] ومجاهد: أمرنا

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وأبو حياة الشامي ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read آمرنا with a long alif, meaning God made the town’s people numerous.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة وأبو حياة الشامي ويعقوب: آمرنا ممدودة أي أكثرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading with kasra means God commanded the affluent to obey, but they disobeyed; it may also mean making leaders or increasing their number.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بكسر الميم، أي أمرناهم بالطاعة فعصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abundance sense is supported by a Prophetic phrase for a mare with many offspring, Labīd’s poem, and Arabic usage of أمر for abundance.
rows.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «خير المال مهرة مأمورة أو سكة مأبورة»

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: They prefer the common reading because its senses include command, leadership, and abundance.
rows.anchor: واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم وقرأه العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town’s affluent and leaders are meant by its mutrafīn; their disobedience makes punishment due, and God utterly destroys them in a wondrous way.
rows.anchor: وهم أغنياؤها ورؤساءها ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: The Prophet warned that a breach had opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog, bringing approaching evil to the Arabs; a community may be destroyed despite righteous people when corruption spreads.
rows.anchor: روى معمر عن الزهري قال: دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of destroyed generations warns the Meccan unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وكم أهلكنا من القرون من بعد نوح تخوف كفار مكة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي
rows.claim: A generation lasts 120 years; the Prophet was sent at its beginning and its last person was Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن أبي: وفي القرن عشرون ومائة سنة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن بشير المازني
rows.claim: The Prophet said a boy would live a generation and defined it as 100 years; the narrator counted until the boy died after a century.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وضع يده على رأسه وقال: «سيعيش هذا الغلام قرنا»

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: A generation lasts eighty years.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: القرن ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: A Prophetic report defines a generation as forty years.
rows.anchor: عن ابن سيرين قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «القرن أربعون سنة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The urgent life means this world; the adjective stands for “the urgent abode.” God grants only what He wills to whom He wills, whether abundance or restriction.
rows.anchor: من كان يريد العاجلة يعني الدنيا فعبرنا بحرف عن الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly seeker eventually enters Hell, disgraced and expelled.
rows.anchor: ثم جعلنا له جهنم في الآخرة يصلاها يدخلها مذموما مدحورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife seeker must strive properly and be a believer; such striving is accepted rather than rejected.
rows.anchor: ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وعمل لها عملها وهو مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies both groups, those seeking this life and those seeking the next.
rows.anchor: كلا نمد هؤلاء وهؤلاء أي نمد كل الفريقين، من يريد العاجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides both groups from His bounty, though their fortunes differ; His provision is not withheld from His servants.
rows.anchor: فيرزقهما جميعا من عطاء ربك ثم يختلف بهما الحال في المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave different ranks in provision and deeds to seekers of this life and the next; the next life has greater ranks and distinction.
rows.anchor: انظر يا محمد كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض في الرزق والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning against another deity is addressed to the Prophet but intended for others; idolatry leaves one disgraced and unsupported.
rows.anchor: الخطاب إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد به غيره فتقعد فتبقى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: In a story about a man blaming triple divorce on God’s decree, Hasan clarified that قَضَى means God commanded, not that He predestined the divorce.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وكان فصيحا: ما قضى الله، أي ما أمر الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: They gloss قَضَى as “enjoined,” supported by a variant reading of ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, and Ubayy.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن زيد: وأوصى ربك، ودليل هذا التأويل

rows.speaker: شريك بن مزاحم
rows.claim: He read وصّى and explained that readers brought wāw near ṣād until it sounded like qāf.
rows.anchor: عن شريك بن مزاحم أنه قرأ: ووصى ربك

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: He interprets the wording as God making filial kindness obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: [وأوجب] ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also commands kindness to parents, treating them with goodness and affection.
rows.anchor: وبالوالدين إحسانا أي وأمر بالأبوين إحسانا برا بهما وعطفا عليهما

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads يبلغن with an alif; other readers omit it and take the verb as singular, with the next phrase starting a new sentence.
rows.anchor: الكسائي بالألف، وقرأ الباقون: يبلغن بغير الألف على الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أف has three recognized readings—fatḥ without tanwīn, kasr with tanwīn, and kasr without tanwīn—and all mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: فيه ثلاث لغات بفتح الفاء [حيث قد رفع] وهي قراءة أهل مكة والشام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: أف is an expression of displeasure.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي كلمة كراهة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: أف means bad, harsh speech.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: الكلام الرديء الغليظ

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Af and taf originally refer to dirt rubbed from the fingers.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيد: أصل الأف والتف الوسخ على الأصابع إذا فتلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations distinguish the terms as sweat and dirt in body folds versus dirt on fingers, ears, or nails, or a worthless thing lifted from the ground.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيد: أصل الأف والتف الوسخ على الأصابع إذا فتلته وفرق الآخرون بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further explanations call أف dirt of the ear or fingernail and تف dirt beneath nails or a worthless thing lifted from the ground.
rows.anchor: الأف ما يكون في المغابن من العرق والوسخ، والتف ما يكون في الأصابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rebuke parents; speak to them kindly and beautifully.
rows.anchor: ولا تنهرهما لا تزجرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما حسنا جميلا

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: A gracious expression to parents is like a sinful servant speaking to a harsh master.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: كقول العبد المذنب للسيد الفظ

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Do not give parents hurtful names or nicknames; address them as father and mother.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: لا تسمهما ولا تكنهما وقل لهما: يا أبتاه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Even if parents become so old that their child must handle their toileting, the child must not shrink from caring for them.
rows.anchor: مجاهد في هذه الآية: إن بلغا عندك من الكبر ما يبولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not express disgust while removing parents’ waste as they removed yours when you were small.
rows.anchor: ولا تقل لهما أف حين ترى الأذى وتميط عنهما الخراء والبول

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: The disobedient child dies a bad death.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن المسيب: أن [العاق] يموت ميتة سوء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Asked whether caring for aged parents repaid them, the Prophet said no: they wanted the child to live, while he acts wishing them dead.
rows.anchor: وقال رجل لرسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) : إن أبوي بلغا من الكبر

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: Humility toward parents means not withholding from them what they wish to have.
rows.anchor: قال عروة بن الزبير: إن لهما حتى لا يمتنع من شيء أحياه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Lowering the wing means softening one’s manner and humbling oneself before parents.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: ألن لهما جانبك فاخضع لهما

rows.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعاصم الجحدري
rows.claim: They read الذل with kasra on dhāl, meaning one should not find serving parents burdensome.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعاصم الجحدري: جناح الذل بكسر الذال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He considers the prayer for parents abrogated by the prohibition on seeking forgiveness for polytheists, even close relatives.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو منسوخ بقوله ما كان للنبي والذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God’s pleasure accompanies parental pleasure and His displeasure accompanies parental displeasure.
rows.anchor: رضى الله تعالى مع رضا الوالدين وسخط الله مع سخط الوالدين

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report warns that the disobedient child will not be forgiven, while the dutiful child may act freely and be forgiven.
rows.anchor: عطاء عن عائشة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يقال للعاق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report promises two gates of Paradise to one who pleases both parents and two gates of Hell to one who displeases them; the Prophet affirmed this even if parents wronged him.
rows.anchor: روى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «من أمسى مرضيا

rows.speaker: أبو عمر القصبي
rows.claim: When asked for a deed that brings one near to God, the Prophet said dutifulness to both parents sufficed with little other work.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمر [القصبي] قال: جاء رجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the inner state regarding parental kindness or disobedience; if people are righteous after a lapse, He forgives those who return from sin.
rows.anchor: ربكم أعلم بما في نفوسكم من بر الوالدين وعقوقهما

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A person acting toward parents spontaneously only out of good will is not held accountable for that impulse.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير في هذه الآية: هو الرجل يكون منه المبادرة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The awābīn are those who return to goodness.
rows.anchor: فقال سعيد بن جبير: الراجعين إلى الخير

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: The awābīn are people who sin and repent repeatedly.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن المسيب: الذي يذنب ثم يتوب ثم يذنب ثم يتوب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They privately remember their sins and ask God to forgive them.
rows.anchor: مجاهد عن عبيد بن عمر: هو الذي يذكر ذنوبه في الخلا

rows.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: They ask God to forgive what they did in a gathering.
rows.anchor: عمرو بن دينار: هو الذي يقول: اللهم اغفر لي ما أصبت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The awābīn are those returning to God; the word follows the pattern فعّال from أوب, to return, as a poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: الراجع إلى الله فيما

rows.speaker: الوالبي
rows.claim: The awābīn are the obedient and humble.
rows.anchor: الوالبي: عنه المطيعين المخبتين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The awābīn are those who pray.
rows.anchor: قتادة: المصلين. عون العقيلي

rows.speaker: عون العقيلي
rows.claim: The awābīn are those who perform the forenoon prayer.
rows.anchor: عون العقيلي: هم الذين يصلون صلاة الضحى

rows.speaker: ابن المنكدر
rows.claim: The awābīn are those who pray between sunset and night prayers.
rows.anchor: ابن المنكدر: بين المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A report describes the awābīn as people who are eager and longing.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: الأوابين الرغابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right of kin means maintaining kinship; some interpret the kin specifically as the Prophet’s relatives.
rows.anchor: يعني صلة الرحم. وقال بعضهم: عني بذلك قرابة رسول الله

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: He told a Syrian visitor that the Prophet’s family are the relatives whose right God commanded people to give.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن الحسين لرجل من أهل الشام أقرأت القرآن؟ قال نعم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wayfarer is a traveler passing through; another view takes him to mean a guest.
rows.anchor: والمسكين وابن السبيل يعني مار الطريق، وقيل: الضيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Squandering means spending wealth on disobedience.
rows.anchor: ولا تنفق مالك في المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God widens or constricts provision; this links to the warning that unrestricted wealth would lead people to transgression.
rows.anchor: إن ربك يبسط يوسع الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر يقتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs buried daughters from fear of poverty; God forbids this and promises provision for parents and children.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أهل الجاهلية كانوا يأدون بناتهم خشية الفاقة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read قتلهم with fatḥ on khāʾ and ṭāʾ and a shortened hamza.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر: بفتح الخاء والطاء والهمزة مقصورة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the word with kasra on khāʾ, fatḥ on ṭāʾ, and a lengthened hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير: بكسر الخاء وفتح الطاء ومد الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining reading has kasra on khāʾ and still ṭāʾ; all readings are synonymous and can be noun or verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون: بكسر الخاء وجزم الطاء، وكلها لغات بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: The Prophet said profession of God’s oneness protects blood and property except where a legal right applies, including adultery after marriage, apostasy, or murder.
rows.anchor: روى حميد عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victim’s heir has authority over the killer and may execute, take blood money, or pardon.
rows.anchor: ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا قوة وولاية على قاتل وليه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: They read تسرف with tāʾ, addressing the killer or possibly the Prophet as representative of later leaders and the community; yāʾ refers to the heir.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف: تسرف بالتاء أي فلا تسرف أيها القاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Excess in retaliation means killing someone other than the killer.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: لا يقتل غير قاتله

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic vengeance sometimes killed a prominent person from the killer’s tribe instead of the actual killer; this excess is forbidden.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وابن زيد: كانت العرب في الجاهلية إذا قتل منهم قتيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls killing someone other than the killer, killing in a pre-Islamic feud, and killing in the Sacred Precinct among the gravest offenses against God.
rows.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «إن من أعتى الناس على الله جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: The prohibition was revealed in Mecca as the first Quranic material on killing while polytheists killed the Prophet’s companions; it forbids retaliation against anyone but the killer and predates the command to fight them.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كان هذا بمكة ونبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بها

rows.speaker: قتادة وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr’s fragment on retaliation is damaged; Qatāda, Ṭāriq ibn Ḥabīb, and Ibn Kaysān explicitly forbid mutilating the killer.
rows.anchor: قتادة وطارق بن حبيب وابن كيسان: [لا يمثل به]

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In “he is supported,” the pronoun refers to the victim’s heir, who may execute, pardon, or take blood money.
rows.anchor: هو المنصور على القاتل [فيدفع الامام] إليه القاتل، فإن شاء قتل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the murdered person, supported by retaliation in this life and repentance in the next.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: (من) راجعة إلى المقتول في قوله ومن قتل مظلوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphan-property prohibition continues until maturity and accountability.
rows.anchor: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلى قوله مسؤلا عنه

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: Kufan readers pronounce قسطاس with kasra on qāf; others use fatḥa. It means a scale, small or large.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة: القسطاس بكسر القاف. الباقون: بفتحه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says قسطاس is the Persian word for justice.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: هو العدل بالرومية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies قسطاس as a steelyard.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو القبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best outcome means the best eventual result.
rows.anchor: ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا أي عاقبة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A Prophetic report promises a better worldly replacement to one who abandons a forbidden act solely from fear of God.
rows.anchor: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا يقدر رجل على حرام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Do not claim to have seen, heard, or known something when you did not; this is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: لا تقل رأيت ولم تر وسمعت ولم تسمعه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Do not accuse anyone of something without knowledge; this is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: ولا ترم أحدا بما ليس لك به علم

rows.speaker: ابن الحنفية
rows.claim: He interprets the prohibition as forbidding false testimony.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الحنفية: هو شهادة الزور

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Do not follow conjecture or suspicion; the explanations converge, and the root q-f-w means slander or false accusation.
rows.anchor: قال [القتيبي] : لا تتبع الحدس والظنون، وكلها متقاربة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying rejects slandering one’s mother and disowning one’s father, using the root under discussion.
rows.anchor: نحن بنو النضر بن كنانة لا نقفوا أمنا ولا ننتفي من أبينا

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line uses التقافيا as evidence for the root q-f-w.
rows.anchor: بهن الحياء لا يشعن التقافيا

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt’s line uses أقفوا as evidence for the word and its sense.
rows.anchor: ولا أقفوا الحواصين أن [قفينا]

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: He derives the word from the nape, describing following things from behind; قفوت أثره means following someone’s trace.
rows.anchor: وقال [القتيبي] : فهو مأخوذ من القفاء كأنه يقفوا الأمور

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ derives it from tracking footprints and argues for ḍamma on qāf, as in ولا تقل; he cites variant Arabic verb forms.
rows.anchor: وحكى الفراء عن بعضهم: أن أصله من القيافة، وهو اتباع الأثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كل أولئك can refer to the named organs or their owners; Jarīr’s verse illustrates the latter usage.
rows.anchor: كل أولئك أي كل هذه الجوارح والأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking مرحًا means arrogant pride and swagger; it explains the walk as a verbal noun, not an adjective.
rows.anchor: بطرا وفخرا وخيلاء، وهو تفسير المشي لا نعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot cross the whole earth; the idiom أخرق الأرض describes a widely traveled person, supported by a Rajaz line.
rows.anchor: يقال فلان أخرق الأرض من فلان إذا كان أكثر سفرا

rows.speaker: روبة
rows.claim: Rawba’s line supplies evidence for مخترق in the sense of a traversed tract.
rows.anchor: وقال روبة: وقائم [الأعماق] خاوي المخترق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot match the mountains’ height or tower over them.
rows.anchor: أي [لن تساويها بطولك ولا تطاولك]

rows.speaker: الحسن ويحيى بن يعمر وابن عمر وأهل الكوفة
rows.claim: They read سيئه in a genitive construction, referring to all the preceding prohibitions beginning with worship of God alone.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن ويحيى بن يعمر وابن عمر وأهل الكوفة: سيئه على الإضافة

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وحمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: They read تسبح with feminine tāʾ; other readers use masculine yāʾ, which Abū ʿUbayd prefers as agreement with the feminine subject.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن: وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وحمزة والكسائي وحفص: بالتاء، غيرهم: يسبح بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God transcendent, obeying Him, affirming His lordship, and demonstrating His existence and oneness.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التسبيح التنزيه والطاعة والالتزام بالربوبية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Every living thing glorifies God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وإن من شيء حي

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: They say every ensouled thing glorifies God.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن والضحاك: يعني كل شيء فيه الروح

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the glorifying things as animals and plants.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني الحيوانات والنباتات

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: A tree glorifies God, whereas a column does not.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: الشجرة تسبح والأسطوانة لا تسبح

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When asked whether a dining table glorifies God, Hasan said it once did.
rows.anchor: فقال يزيد الرقاشي يا أبا سعيد يسبح هذا الخوان؟ فقال كان يسبح مرة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Food glorifies God.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم: الطعام يسبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A damaged Prophetic report says a staff ceased glorifying after it had glorified.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: « [ما سبحت عصا إلا ترك] التسبيح»

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet taught that Noah instructed his son to say Glory and praise be to God, creation’s prayer and glorification and a means of provision.
rows.anchor: يا بني آمرك أن تقول: سبحان الله وبحمده فإنها صلاة الخلق وتسبيحهم

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: A damaged report says that every unidentified thing had glorified God for three hundred years.
rows.anchor: إلا وقد كان يسبح لله ثلاثمائة سنة

rows.speaker: المقداد بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: A report says soil glorifies before wetting, nuts before moving, leaves on trees, water while unchanged, clothes when new, and animals while vocalizing.
rows.anchor: عن المقداد بن معد يكرب قال: إن التراب يسبح ما لم يبتل

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Pebbles glorified in the Prophet’s hand and in Abū Bakr’s, ʿUmar’s, and ʿUthmān’s, but not in the Companions’ hands.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخذ كفا من حصى

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: A report says grapes and pomegranates glorified when the Prophet, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and ʿAlī ate, but not when an ordinary Companion did.
rows.anchor: وعن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه قال: «مرض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأتاه جبرئيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People do not understand other things’ glorification because it is not expressed in their own languages and tongues.
rows.anchor: يعني لا تعلمون تسبيح ما عدا من تسبيح بلغاتكم وألسنتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet recites the Quran to polytheists, God places a veil between them that blocks their hearts from understanding and benefiting from it.
rows.anchor: وإذا قرأت القرآن يا محمد [على] المشركين جعلنا بينك بينهم حجابا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He glosses حجابًا مستورًا as a covering barrier; مستور is passive in form but active in sense, like مأتيا in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: قتادة: هو حجاب مستور، والمستور يعني الساتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the barrier is unseen by people; another interpretation identifies it as the Quran, unseen and inaccessible as evidence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه مستورا عن أعين الناس فلا يرونه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: When Abū Lahab’s wife came to abuse the Prophet, he said a barrier would be placed; an angel screened him so she could not see him.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إنه سيحال بيني وبينها» فلم تره

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the Prophet concealed himself from polytheists by reciting passages from al-Kahf, al-Naḥl, and al-Jāthiya.
rows.anchor: قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يستتر من المشركين بثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: People who recited those passages escaped persecutors who could not see them, in Syria and near Rayy.
rows.anchor: ثم قرأ بهن فخرج هاربا وخرجوا في طلبه حتى كانوا يكونون على طريقه ولا يبصرونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet recites the declaration of God’s oneness alone in the Quran, the polytheists turn away in aversion.
rows.anchor: وإذا قلت: لا إله إلا الله في القرآن وحده وأنت تتلوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says those who turn away are devils; نفور is a plural like قعود or جلوس, or a verbal noun meaning flight.
rows.anchor: حدثنا أبو الجوزاء عن ابن عباس في قوله ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا قال: هم الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan leaders secretly called the Prophet mad, a soothsayer, sorcerer, or poet while listening to his Quran recitation.
rows.anchor: وإذ هم نجوى متناجون في أمرك، بعضهم يقول: هو مجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bewitched-man accusation is attributed to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and companions after Meccans consulted him.
rows.anchor: بمعنى الوليد بن المغيرة وأصحابه حين رجع إليه كفار مكة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: مسحور can mean a man with lungs who eats and drinks like others; an Imruʾ al-Qays line uses سحر for being fed.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: [مسحورا] يعني رجلا له سحر يأكل ويشرب مثلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their comparisons led them astray, leaving them unable to find an exit or the path of truth.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: شاعر وساحر وكاهن ومجنون فضلوا فجالوا وجاروا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses رفات as dust.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: غبارا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He glosses رفات as soil; it also means crushed and decayed fragments like crumbs or rubble.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: ترابا، والرفات ما تكسر وبلا من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything too great for people to imagine reviving is included; views include what follows death, heaven and earth, resurrection, or death itself.
rows.anchor: يعني خلقا مما يكبر عندكم عن قبول الحياة وبعثكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: They identify the greatest thing people can imagine as death; even if people became death, God would still resurrect them.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد وعكرمة في قوله أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم قالا: الموت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In another report he says heaven, earth, and mountains; whatever people become, God can make them die and resurrect them.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: السماء والأرض والجبال يقول كونوا ما شئتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers move their heads in amazement and mockery; نغضت سنه describes a tooth that moves and loosens at its root.
rows.anchor: فسينغضون إليك رؤسهم أي يحركون رؤوسهم متعجبين ومستهزئين

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz line supplies poetic evidence for the head movement expressed by نغض.
rows.anchor: أبغض نحوي رأسه وأقنعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two further lines, one attributed to al-Ḥajjāj, are cited as poetic witnesses to the same movement; the last line is damaged.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: لما رأسني الغضت لي الرأسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God says the Hour may be near, may means certainty; the commentary links the expression with two other verses.
rows.anchor: يعني هو قريب لأن عسى من الله واجب نظيره قوله لعل الساعة تكون قريبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is from graves to the gathering place of Judgment, and people respond with praise.
rows.anchor: يوم يدعوكم من قبوركم إلى [موقف يوم القيامة] فتستجيبون بحمده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets responding with praise as responding to God’s command.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بأمره

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets it as responding through knowledge and obedience, praising God as worthy of praise.
rows.anchor: قتادة: بمعرفته وطاعته، ويحمدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection people think their worldly stay was only a short time.
rows.anchor: وتظنون إن لبثتم في الدنيا في قبولكم إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: ابن عمرو
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says monotheists face no fear in their graves or gathering and praise God for removing sorrow.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمرو أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ليس على أهل لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says an Arab insulted ʿUmar and God ordered him to pardon the man.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب، وذلك أن رجلا من العرب شتمه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Another says polytheists verbally and physically harmed the Companions, who complained to the Prophet, and the verse came in response.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: كان المشركون يؤذون أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقول والفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should answer unbelievers with the best words rather than repay them in kind; Hasan suggests praying that God guide and show mercy, before fighting was commanded.
rows.anchor: يقولوا للكافرين التي هي أحسن يعني الكلمة التي هي أحسن لا تكافئهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the best word is the confession of God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأحسن كلمة الإخلاص لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan incites conflict by whispering and casting enmity between people.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم يفتري، وألقى بينهما العداوة

rows.speaker: ابن حريج
rows.claim: God may guide people to faith and mercy, or let them die in polytheism and punish them.
rows.anchor: إن يشأ يعذبكم يميتكم على الشرك فيعذبكم، قاله ابن حريج

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Alternatively, mercy means protecting people from Mecca, while punishment means giving the Meccans power over them.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: إن الله يرحمكم فيحفظكم من أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Prophet is not their guardian or guarantor was abrogated by the fighting verse.
rows.anchor: وما أرسلناك عليهم وكيلا وكفيلا، نسختها آية القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows heavenly and earthly creatures and made people differ in character, circumstances, and affairs.
rows.anchor: فجعلهم مختلفين في أخلاقهم من أمورهم وأحوالهم ومالهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda lists distinctions among prophets: Abraham as intimate friend, Moses spoken to, Jesus created by command, Solomon granted a kingdom, David given Psalms, and Muhammad forgiven.
rows.anchor: قتادة: في هذه الآية اتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا، وكلم الله موسى تكليما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David’s Psalms contained prayer, praise, and glorification, but no laws, obligations, or legal limits.
rows.anchor: وآتى داود زبورا كتابا علمه داود فيه دعاء وتحميد وتمجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supposed gods cannot remove or transfer harm; it may refer to the seven-year famine that struck the Meccans.
rows.anchor: فلا يملكون كشف الضر عنكم ولا تحويلا [عنكم] إلى غيركم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A reading transmitted by Qatāda has تبتغون with tāʾ instead of the common يبتغون with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ أولئك الذين يدعون تبتغون بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wasīla is nearness to God; those seeking it hope for His mercy and fear His punishment.
rows.anchor: إلى ربهم الوسيلة القربة إلى ربهم أيهم أقرب إليه ويرجون رحمته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأكثر العلماء
rows.claim: The beings people invoke—Jesus, his mother, Ezra, angels, sun, moon, and stars—are themselves seeking nearness to God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وأكثر العلماء: هم عيسى وأمه وعزير والملائكة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Some humans worshipped jinn who later embraced Islam without their human worshippers knowing; the humans persisted in worship and were corrected by the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: كان نفر من الإنس يعبدون نفرا من الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every town will be destroyed or harshly punished before Judgment for disbelief and disobedience; some say this is universal, with the righteous dying and the wicked punished.
rows.anchor: وإن من قرية يعني وما من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The righteous meet destruction through death, while the wicked receive punishment.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: أما الصالح فبالموت وأما الطالح فبالعذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: If adultery and usury spread in a town, God permits its destruction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إذا ظهر الزنا والربا في أهل قرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This decree is written in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك في الكتاب في اللوح المحفوظ مسطورا مكتوبا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Meccans asked for Ṣafā to become gold; God offered to grant the request or delay, warning that denial of a sign would bring destruction, and the Prophet chose to wait.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قال أهل مكة: اجعل لنا الصفا ذهبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel was a clear sign; the Thamūd acknowledged its divine origin but wronged it by rejecting it.
rows.anchor: وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة مضيئة بينة فظلموا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs are sent as warnings so people believe, remember, and return; otherwise they are punished.
rows.anchor: وما نرسل بالآيات بالعبر والدلالات إلا تخويفا للعباد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: God warns with whatever signs He wills, hoping people awaken or return; after a Kūfa earthquake, Ibn Masʿūd urged them to repent.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: إن الله يخوف الناس بما شاء من آياته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets the warning signs as rapid, widespread death.
rows.anchor: وروى محمد بن يوسف عن الحسن في قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators say God controls and protects the Prophet from people, so he should proceed fearlessly with his message.
rows.anchor: فهم في قبضته لا يقدرون على الخروج من مشيئته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God’s encompassing means His knowledge includes everyone and nothing is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني أحاط علمه بهم فلا يخفى عليه منهم شيء

rows.speaker: مقاتل والبراء
rows.claim: They take the encompassed people as the Meccans and understand the promise as saying Mecca will be opened to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: مقاتل والبراء: أحاط بالناس يعني أهل مكة أي أنها ستفتح لك

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن ومسروق وأبو مالك وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك وابن زيد وابن جريج وعطية وعكرمة
rows.claim: They interpret the vision as an actual waking sight of the Night Journey’s wonders; it tested people, some of whom denied or apostatized while others believed.
rows.anchor: قال قوم: هي رؤيا عين وهو ما أرى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: معاوية
rows.claim: Asked about the night journey, Muʿāwiya called it a true vision from God, meaning a sight witnessed with the eyes.
rows.anchor: حديث معاوية أنه كان إذا سئل عن مسرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the vision was the Prophet’s spirit-only night journey; some Muslims doubted it and hypocrites attacked it.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي ما أرى الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة أسرى بروحه

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: In the Prophet’s vision, a man who rejected the Quran and neglected obligatory prayer repeatedly had his head smashed by a rock and restored.
rows.anchor: فإذا رجل مستلقي على قفاه ورجل قائم بيده صخرة فشدخ بها رأسه

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: A habitual liar had his cheek, eye, and nostril torn back to his neck, then restored for repeated punishment.
rows.anchor: فإذا آخر قائم عليه بكلوب من حديد فإذا هو يأخذ أحد شقي وجهه

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: Naked men and women in an oven-like house were adulterers and adulteresses.
rows.anchor: فإذا فيه رجال ونساء عراة وإذا هم يأتيهم لهب من أسفل منهم

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: A man swimming in a river of blood and forced to swallow stones was a consumer of usury.
rows.anchor: فأتينا على نهر من دم أحمر وإذا في البحر سابح يسبح

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: The ugly man tending fire was Mālik, keeper of Hell; the tall man in the garden was Abraham, surrounded by children born upon the natural disposition.
rows.anchor: وأما الرجل الكريه المرأة الذي عنده النار يحشها فإنه مالك خازن النار

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: People partly beautiful and partly ugly had mixed righteous and evil deeds and were pardoned; the garden was Eden and the city was the abode of martyrs.
rows.anchor: فإنهم قوم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا فتجاوز الله عنهم

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: Gabriel and Michael showed the Prophet his unfinished home and said he would enter it if he completed his term.
rows.anchor: قالا لي: ها هو ذا منزلك، وأنا جبرئيل وهذا ميكائيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The vision was the Prophet’s dream that he and his companions would enter Mecca at al-Ḥudaybiya; after the Meccans turned them back and some doubted, they entered the following year as foretold.
rows.anchor: وروى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: هي رؤيا التي رأى أنه يدخل مكة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: The Prophet saw the Umayyads on pulpits and was saddened; the vision was a worldly trial whose worldly share was withheld from him.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب، من قول الله تعالى وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet saw the Umayyads leaping on his pulpit like monkeys, was saddened, and the cursed tree means Zaqqūm.
rows.anchor: قال: رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بني أمية ينزون على منبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cursed tree is Zaqqūm; grammatically it is coordinated with the vision, and both were made a trial.
rows.anchor: الشجرة الملعونة المذكورة في القرآن يعني شجرة الزقوم

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abū Jahl mocked that a tree could grow in fire; al-Zibari said zaqqūm meant dates and butter in Berber, which Abū Jahl served to ridicule the warning.
rows.anchor: أن أبا جهل قال- لما نزلت هذه الآية: أليس من الكذب ابن أبي كبشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran answers the mockery by describing Zaqqūm as sinners’ food growing in Hell, created from and suited to fire.
rows.anchor: إن شجرة الزقوم طعام الأثيم ووصفها في الصافات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In response to a question, he says the cursed tree is the parasitic plant that winds around other trees, called الكشوث.
rows.anchor: إلى ابن عباس: نحن الشجرة الملعونة في القرآن؟ قال: فقال: الشجرة الملعونة هي هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis objected to prostrating to Adam because Adam was created from clay.
rows.anchor: فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا يعني من طين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Iblis brought sweet and salty earth to create Adam; the sweet portion yields bliss and the salty wretchedness regardless of parentage, and Adam’s name derives from earth’s surface.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: بعث رب العزة إبليس فأخذ كفا من أديم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis says he will seize, overcome, and destroy most descendants through misguidance; the word also evokes taking all of something or leading an animal by its jaw.
rows.anchor: لأحتنكن ذريته أي لأستولين على أولاده ولأحتوينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The few exempt from Iblis’s reach are the protected, as stated later of God’s servants.
rows.anchor: إلا قليلا يعني المعصومين الذين استثناهم الله في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment due to Iblis and his followers is complete and abundant.
rows.anchor: فإن جهنم جزاؤكم أي جزاءك وجزاء أتباعك جزاء موفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استفزز means dominate, unsettle, mislead, or entice whichever descendants of Adam Satan can reach.
rows.anchor: واستفزز [استولي] واستخف واستزل واستمل من استطعت منهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Satan’s voice is his invitation to sin; any caller to disobedience belongs to his troops.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: بدعائك إلى معصية الله وكل داع إلى معصية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets Satan’s voice as singing and musical instruments.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بالغناء والمزامير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أجلب عليهم means to gather and shout against them; Muqātil offers an alternative gloss.
rows.anchor: وأجلب عليهم أي اجمع وصح. مقاتل: استفز عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s cavalry and infantry include everyone riding or walking in disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: كل راكب وماش في معاصي الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Satan has cavalry and infantry among jinn and humans; mounted fighters in disobedience are his cavalry and those on foot his infantry.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة: إن له خيلا ورجلا من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads رجلك with kasra on rāʾ; the two forms are dialect variants like راكب and ركب.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص: ورجلك بكسر الراء، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Satan shares in wealth acquired unlawfully and spent unlawfully; this is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعبد الرحمن بن زيد

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: He identifies Satan’s share in wealth as usury.
rows.anchor: عطاء بن أبي رباح: هو الربا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says Satan shares through livestock practices the polytheists declared sacred, including baḥīra, sāʾiba, waṣīla, and ḥāmī.
rows.anchor: قتادة: ما كان المشركون يحرمونه من الأنعام كالبحائر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says Satan’s share includes animals slaughtered for idols.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو ما كان يذبحونه لآلهتهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Some interpret Satan’s share in offspring as children conceived through fornication; this is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: وهو قول مجاهد والضحاك

rows.speaker: الوالبي
rows.claim: He interprets the offspring share as accepting forbidden practices for one’s children.
rows.anchor: الوالبي عنه: هو ما قبلوا من أولادهم

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Satan participates in offspring by leading families to make children Zoroastrian, Jewish, or Christian.
rows.anchor: الحسن وقتادة: عدو الله شاركهم في أموالهم وأولادهم فمجسوا وهودوا

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Satan shares in offspring when parents name a child ʿAbd al-Ḥārith, ʿAbd Shams, or a similar name.
rows.anchor: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس: مشاركته إياهم في الأولاد وتسميتهم أولادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s promises are false and cannot save people from punishment; the commentary links this with his admission that God’s promise was true.
rows.anchor: وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا باطلا وخديعة لأنه لا يغني عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes ships to glide across the sea for people to seek His bounty; يزجي means to set them moving.
rows.anchor: لكم الفلك في البحر إلى قوله وإذا مسكم الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At sea in distress and fear of drowning, people invoke only God; after rescue to land they turn from faith and obedience, displaying ingratitude.
rows.anchor: وإذا مسكم الضر أصابكم [الجهد] في البحر وخفتم الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those rescued at sea should not feel safe from sinking on land or a hail of stones like that sent on Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: أن يخسف بكم يغيبكم ويذهبكم في جانب البر أو يرسل عليكم حاصبا حجارة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد والقتيبي
rows.claim: They define حاصب as a storm that throws small pebbles.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد والقتيبي: الحاصب الذي يرمي بالحصباء

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line uses بحاصب to describe a scattered shower of small stones.
rows.anchor: قال الفرزدق: مستقبلين شمال الشام يضربنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: قاصف is a violent wind that crushes things, including trees; تبيع means a helper or avenger.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقال أبو عبيدة: هي التي تقصف كل شيء أي تدقه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read all four verbs with first-person plural nūn, in agreement with علينا.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: نخسف ونرسل ونعيدكم ونغرقكم كلها بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readers use third-person yāʾ to match إياه; Abū Jaʿfar reads تغرقكم with tāʾ, making the wind its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: كلها بالياء لقوله (إياه)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation is that humans eat with their hands while other creatures eat with their mouths; another says human honor is reason.
rows.anchor: ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس في قوله ولقد كرمنا بني آدم قال: كل شيء يأكل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says God honored humans with speech and discernment.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: بالنطق وثم التمييز

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ identifies human honor as upright, proportioned stature.
rows.anchor: عطاء: تعديل العامة وامتدادها

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: Yamān says humans were honored with beautiful form.
rows.anchor: يمان: بحسن الصورة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says humanity was honored by God making Muhammad one of them.
rows.anchor: محمد بن كعب: بأن جعل محمدا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view points to men’s beards and women’s tresses as forms of distinction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الرجال باللحي والنساء بالذواب

rows.speaker: محمد بن جرير
rows.claim: Humans are honored by being empowered over other creatures and having creation subjected to them.
rows.anchor: محمد بن جرير: بتسليطهم على غيرهم من الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good provisions are pleasant foods and drinks; Muqātil names ghee, butter, dates, and sweets.
rows.anchor: ورزقناهم من الطيبات يعني لذيذ المطاعم والمشارب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He names clarified butter, butter, dates, and sweets as human provisions.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: السمن والزبد والتمر والحلاوى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: One view reads “many” as all creatures except some angels; al-Kalbī names Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, the Angel of Death, and similar angels.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: فضلوا على الخلائق كلهم غير طائفة من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others take “many” rhetorically as all, as in the cited verse where “most” refers to all devils.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: المراد به جميع من خلقنا

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Angels asked why Adam’s descendants received worldly food while angels did not; God swore not to equate those made by His hands with those created by His command Be.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، في قوله تعالى ولقد كرمنا بني آدم قال: قالت: الملائكة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra says a believer is more honored with God than the angels near Him.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: المؤمن أكرم على الله من الملائكة الذين عنده

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: They say each nation is called with its prophet; a Prophetic report from Abū Hurayra supports this.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: بنبيهم، يدل عليه ما روى السدي

rows.speaker: أبو صالح وأبو نضر والضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: They say each nation is called with its revealed book; another report says each people comes with its era’s imam, scripture, and the Prophet’s practice.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح وأبو نضر والضحاك وابن زيد: بكتابهم الذي أنزل عليهم

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says each people is brought with the imam of its time, scripture, and the Prophet’s sunna.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يوم ندعوا كل أناس بإمامهم قال: «يؤتى كل قوم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية والحسن
rows.claim: They say nations are called with their deeds, supported by the following reference to receiving the book in the right hand and a verse naming the record an imam.
rows.anchor: أبو العالية والحسن: بأعمالهم، ودليل هذا التأويل قوله تعالى في سياق الآية

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report says people giving paired things for God are called through Paradise’s gate matching their worship; Abū Bakr asks if one can be called through all gates, and the Prophet hopes he will.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من أنفق زوجين في سبيل الله نودي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A nation may be called with the leader who called it to guidance or misguidance in worldly life.
rows.anchor: باذان وسعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: بإمامهم الذي دعاهم في الدنيا
